summary: Rook Island light at the mouth of Queensport harbour: first lit 1882, present building 1936, seventeen keepers, de-staffed 1967, heritage lighthouse since 2015.

structures.note: Lighthouse and keeper's dwelling combined; two storeys with a square lantern. Register gives 12.5 m (41 ft); NSLPS gives 41 ft.
Built by James McDonald of Guysborough; replaced 1936 or 1937.

staffing.note: De-staffed for good in 1967 (LighthouseFriends); automated by 1967 (NSLPS).

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends visitor note). NSLPS: site access by boat. Roadside pullout on Route 16 towards Canso offers a view (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Municipality of the District of Guysborough (maintenance since 1979, per LighthouseFriends)
facts.ownership_note: NSLPS: Owned by the Municipality of Guysborough. LighthouseFriends visitor note: owned by the Canadian Coast Guard (out of date).

events.note: Light placed in operation 25 November 1882 by keeper John Ehler III
James McDonald of Guysborough built the square tapered tower and attached dwelling under a $1,429 contract
Foundation cemented; new stays fitted to the tower
Hand-operated foghorn supplied to keeper David S. Hensbee; Crow Harbour listed among stations whose hand fog-horns sound whenever vessels' fog signals are heard
Department's place-name changes record Crow harbour renamed Queensport
Present lighthouse and dwelling built (register). NSLPS gives 1937.
NSLPS: replaced tower of 1882 (dates the present building 1937)
Notice to Mariners, 8 December 1955: fixed white to flashing white; hand foghorn discontinued; light unwatched
De-staffed for good in 1967; automated by 1967
Boathouse and oil shed declared surplus in April 1968, sold and removed within two months
Lighthouse declared surplus and offered for sale for $1,000 on condition of removal; Fishermen's Lighthouse Association negotiated a five-year lease to develop the island as a historic site and park
Placed on the Canadian Register of Historic Places in 2005 (LighthouseFriends)
Recognised as a Heritage Lighthouse on 12 February 2015 (register)
NSLPS history for the first light: 'replaced by present tower' in an entry for 1955 to 1962 (the register gives 1936 and NSLPS's list gives 1937 for the present building)

corrections.why: The record's point is from OpenStreetMap. The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights (H3456) gives 45 20 52.6 N, 061 16 18.9 W, which LighthouseFriends also gives. Difference about 20 m. Reviewer to confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Heritage Guide give 1936; NSLPS gives 1937 and also a 1955 to 1962 date for the replacement. The story gives the register's 1936, NSLPS's 1937 and NSLPS's 1955 to 1962 entry, and does not choose between them.

NSLPS says the Municipality of Guysborough owns it. LighthouseFriends' visitor note says the Coast Guard owns it, but its own history says the municipality has maintained it since 1979. The record names Keepers of the Beacon as agency, which LighthouseFriends mentions as a group working to preserve the lighthouse. The story treats the municipality as the working owner and the group as the preservation body.

LighthouseFriends dates the change of Crow Harbour to Queensport to 1898 (Diamond Jubilee). The Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1901 lists the change among its place-name items. Both are reported.

NSLPS's keeper list spells several keepers differently (Munro, Curtis; Hendsbee, Lawrence; Carter, John; Matheson, Bill; Munro, Ainsley to 1967; Creamer, Austin). The story follows LighthouseFriends' list, which gives Austine R. Creamer as the last keeper to 1967.

notes_for_editor: Built on LighthouseFriends (keeper list of seventeen, and the fact details), the register text (Heritage Guide and HistoricPlaces.ca 20773), NSLPS, the Coast Guard List of Lights (H3456), and two Marine reports from the corpus. The 1955 Notice to Mariners and the 1979 lease are known only through LighthouseFriends. Storms and wrecks: little is sourced; the chapter is the fog-signal duty only. The 1911 Marine casualty tables in the corpus contain a 'Norway ... stranded near Queensport' line that could not be read reliably in the OCR columns; check the page image before adding any wreck. The 1911 Marine keeper table (scan p. 259, printed p. 257) was checked against the page image on 2026-10-27: the Queensport row reads W. E. Ehler, appointed Aug. 13, 1906, salary $385, which agrees with LighthouseFriends' 1906 start; not cited in the story. Record checks: tower height 10.7 m in the record conflicts with 12.5 m (register and NSLPS 41 ft); record's 1936 date agrees with the register. Rook Island boat access is not confirmed in any source read. The Keepers of the Beacon Canadian Digital Collection (hosted by Library and Archives Canada) was not read because LAC's robots rules block the collection's search. Pre-1900 Canadian reports are not in the corpus, so the 1882 construction and keeper appointment facts rest on LighthouseFriends. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story now gives the register's 1936, NSLPS's 1937 and NSLPS's 1955 to 1962 entry without choosing; states NSLPS site access as by boat; dates the fog-horn report to its December 1900 transmittal (the text read gives the month and year); reports the name change to Queensport against LighthouseFriends' 1898 date, noting the Department lists it in the year to 30 June 1901, and does not reconcile the two; removes 'Fog was the hazard the station answered' as general context; names Darryl Spidell only as a local resident; and adds the footnote for the 1900 foghorn. About a dozen LighthouseFriends passages were reworded under the copyright rule. The 1911 casualty table entry (Norway, stranded near Queensport) was not used.
